title: A bash installer copies a tiny tool into a prefix inside the work directory
threat_model: No attacker. A user unpacks a small tarball and runs its bash install.sh, which copies a script into prefix/bin, makes it executable, writes a config under prefix/etc and runs the installed tool.
notes: Everything stays under the work directory under /opt, so no persistence path and no temporary directory is involved. Predicted: no alert. The installed tool is a script that starts with #!/bin/sh, so the processes under the action are only shells of one family, which interpreter_chain does not alert on, and the action needs no timeout wrapper.
